source.author: verg
source.text: Quin, ubi transmissae steterint trans aequora classes, et positis aris iam vota in litore solves, purpureo velare comas adopertus amictu, ne qua inter sanctos ignis in honore deorum hostilis facies occurrat et omina turbet.
source.text_original: Quin, ubi transmissae steterint trans aequora classes, / et positis aris iam vota in litore solves, / purpureo velare comas adopertus amictu, / ne qua inter sanctos ignis in honore deorum / hostilis facies occurrat et omina turbet.
source.text_english: Rather, when the fleets have crossed and stood beyond the seas, and when you shall have set up altars and are now to pay your vows on the shore, cover your hair, veiled in a purple robe, lest any hostile face should meet you among the sacred fires in honor of the gods and disturb the omens.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Vel certe sacerdotes semper operire capita sua debent, juxta illud Virgilianum Aeneid. lib. III: Purpureo velare comas, adopertus amictu.
reuse.text_original: Vel certe sacerdotes semper operire capita sua debent, juxta illud Virgilianum (Aeneid. lib. III): Purpureo velare comas, adopertus amictu.
reuse.text_english: Or certainly priests ought always to cover their heads, according to that line of Virgil in Aeneid, book 3: Cover your hair with purple, wrapped in a robe.
